summary: Jackson County lookout 3 miles north of Butte Falls: a 30-foot tower on Fredenburg Butte, dated 1935 or 1937, removed 1969; staffed 1936-41.

facts.design: 30-foot wooden L-4 tower with a 14x14 cabin
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1969 (firelookout.com says destroyed); the ground cabin was torn down in 1960

staffing.status: lookouts recorded in 1936 and 1941; post deactivated June 14, 1943

events.note: cupola-style lookout house on the butte; firelookout.com lists a D-6 cupola cabin in 1920
forty-foot round-pole tower with 14x14 cabin, per a Rogue River National Forest history quoted by Forest Lookouts; the register and firelookout.com date the 30-foot tower to 1937
Mrs. Ira Tungate at the lookout station when she discovered a 30-acre fire on Ginger Creek in August
Charles (Jiggs) Shepardson employed as lookout; released from duty September 21
listed as part of the Roseburg Filter Center from September 11, 1942
deactivated June 14, 1943; a June 15, 1943 letter says the engineer understood the Rogue River forest had marked it for elimination

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Rogue River National Forest history, quoted by Forest Lookouts, dates the round-pole tower to 1935. The register and firelookout.com date the 30-foot tower to 1937. The story reports both dates.
The register, firelookout.com and the 1942 Forest Service memo give 30 feet (9.1 m). The 1935 history quoted by Forest Lookouts says forty feet. The record keeps 30 feet.
The register says the lookout was removed in 1969. firelookout.com says destroyed. The story uses removed and notes the other word.

notes_for_editor: Brief record confirmed: gone, 30 ft (9.1 m), FFLOS registration December 18, 2010. Build year (1935 vs 1937) and height (30 vs 40 ft) disagree across sources and the story reports both. No source describes the site today or its public access, so access is omitted. Photo credits (Howard Verschoor, Ron Kemnow) appear on the register and firelookout pages but no image URLs were read, so no photos are recorded. Forest Lookouts page cites Medford Mail Tribune and Southwest Oregon District annual reports; those original clippings were not read.
